archetypes.name: shell-cleanup
archetypes.rationale: Diff adds new scout temp file variables to two launchers; every failure exit path must include them in rm -f cleanup and write_status_file must never see SCOUT_WRITTEN unset.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit all exit paths in launch-claude-drafter.sh and launch-codex-drafter.sh for completeness of temp-file cleanup after adding scout_candidate and scout_filtered variables. Enumerate every rm -f call in each script and verify the new scout temp paths appear in CODEX_EXEC_FAILED, CODEX_EMPTY_OUTPUT, parse-failure, and success branches. Check that SCOUT_WRITTEN is initialized to false before any write_status_file invocation that could be reached before the scout filter block runs. Look for any path where a scout temp file could be created but not cleaned up on an abnormal exit. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-protocol
archetypes.rationale: The new SCOUT_WRITTEN/SCOUT_FAIL_REASON KVs and --pre-scouted-manifest threading cross four script layers; each layer's emission and forwarding contract must be consistent and complete.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that SCOUT_WRITTEN and SCOUT_FAIL_REASON are emitted by write_status_file and emit_kv on every non-prelaunch exit path in both drafter launchers, including early error exits before the drafter runs. Check that the --pre-scouted-manifest flag introduced in dispatch-panel.sh and review-core.sh cannot fall through to the legacy scout-dynamic-archetypes.sh launch when a supplied manifest is invalid or fully filtered. Trace the flag threading from run-step5-review.sh through review-and-fix.sh and review-core.sh to dispatch-panel.sh and confirm the flag is forwarded in all orchestrator-mode branches but absent from standalone apply mode. Look for any path where a valid pre-scouted manifest would not trigger dynamic slot synthesis. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: generated-alignment
archetypes.rationale: rendering.py _implementer_text() changes must produce output byte-for-byte matching the hand-edited codex-implementer.md and cursor-implementer.md; test assertions must be tight enough to catch drift.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the rendering.py _implementer_text() codex and cursor branches against the corresponding diff hunks in agents/codex-implementer.md and agents/cursor-implementer.md, verifying that the SCOUT_MANIFEST_PATH bullet text, the revised 'Your output channels' sentence, and the best-effort scout contract paragraph are character-for-character identical between the generator and the generated files. Inspect the new test_generated_implementers_include_scout_sidecar test in test_rendering.py and assess whether its assertions (simple substring checks on short strings) are specific enough to catch future rendering drift without false negatives from generic strings also appearing in unrelated sections. Note any mismatch between what rendering.py would generate and what the hand-edited files contain. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
